newsitem.title: UK: Hungary's MBFB seeks improved terms for loan - LPC.
newsitem.headline: Hungary's MBFB seeks improved terms for loan - LPC.

text.p: LONDON, November 6 (LPC) - Hungarian Bank for Investment and Development (MBFB) is now in general syndication seeking a $60 million term loan package on vastly improved terms, arranger Commerzbank announced.
The credit, split into a $40 million, four year tranche and a $20 million, five year tranche, is priced at 35 bps over LIBOR.

This spread represents a steep drop from MBFB's last loan syndication exercise. In August, the bank raised $50 million through an international syndicate for 3.5 years at a margin over LIBOR of 80 bps.
This is part of a trend among Hungarian borrowers, which are benefiting from the country's improving credit profile and banks' eagerness to lend in the region.
Standard & Poor's raised Hungary's foreign currency debt rating to BBB minus on October 28, citing the country's reduced external debt burden and increasingly dynamic export base.

An oversupply of bank funds is also playing a role in the drop, bankers say. Banks are keen to lend in Hungary not only because it is now a better risk but because it offers better returns than lending in western Europe, where lending margins are at the bottom of a two year swoon.
Commerzbank has approached a small number of MBFB's relationship banks to participate in the facility. Replies are sought by November 20.
